subject: Post-call: Dedicated capacity performance / SLO follow-up
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Sara Blake <sara.blake@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 15:10:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call: Dedicated capacity performance / SLO follow-up

Hi Sara / Tim — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment on performance SLOs and validation plan: 

What we heard (please correct if I got anything wrong):
- Target p95 latency: <= 250 ms for short prompts (<128 tokens) for production traffic; target tighter for streaming partials (aim p95 per-chunk <= 80 ms).
- Concurrency: sustained 60 concurrent user sessions, burst up to 120 for short windows.
- Average generation: ~120–180 tokens per request; 20–30 tps per request expected for your workloads in peak scenarios.
- Streaming required: yes — you want partial tokens as they generate (low time-to-first-token is critical).

What we'll validate / propose:
1) Dedicated capacity sizing with two GPU families (H100 80GB and A100 80GB) — we'll run short perf sweeps to show reserved throughput and p95 streaming latency at your target concurrency.
2) Recommended reserved throughput per GPU (tokens/sec and concurrent requests we can sustain while meeting p95).
3) Autoscale/fallback plan and a mixed-pool option if needed for cost/capacity tradeoffs.

Attachments: capacity_plan_v3.xlsx (capacity/price bands), perf_matrix.pdf (initial perf numbers for representative models).

Immediate asks for you: please confirm the p95 targets above, a representative sample workload/traffic pattern (we can take a small sample or you can share a synthetic profile), and whether any requests must include deterministic streaming behavior (chunk size, flush cadence).

Next steps I propose:
- If you confirm, we’ll schedule a 48-hour validation run (shared-dev infra + dedicated test pool) with both H100 and A100 configs and provide per-GPU reserved throughput numbers, cost estimates, and a recommendation for the production pool size to meet your SLOs.
- Tech deep-dive with Dev and Marissa next week to finalize test harness and metrics to collect (latency histograms, token/sec, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate).

I’ll follow up with a proposed run plan once you confirm.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks, Aditya — this is a great summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- p95 latency target: <= 250 ms for responses where prompt + generation <= 128 tokens. For longer generations we're OK up to ~500 ms p95, but streaming time-to-first-byte (TTFB) should be under 120 ms.
- Streaming behavior: we require streaming for our chat UI. Ideally chunks every ~40 tokens or on sentence boundaries; per-chunk p95 should be <= 80 ms as you noted.
- Concurrency/throughput: sustained 60 concurrent sessions with average 140 tokens per session; bursts to 120 concurrent sessions for short periods (5–10 minutes). Approximate token throughput target: 140 tokens * 60 sessions * average 0.5 requests/minute = ~4200 tokens/min sustained, burst up to ~8400 tokens/min.
- Cost: please include a ballpark monthly cost for a dedicated H100 pool sized to meet the sustained SLO and a mixed pool with A100 fallbacks.

We can share a 24-hour sample of our production traffic (anonymized) — I’ll attach the sample workload. Also two asks for the perf run: include KV cache warmup behavior (we expect a warm cache within the first 30 minutes of a run) and show p95 for streaming and non-streaming modes.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — if possible we’d like the validation run during the week starting July 5.

Best,
Sara Blake
Head of AI Products | Acme Retail
sara.blake@acme-retail.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Dedicated capacity performance / SLO follow-up

Looping in a quick internal plan and proposed sizing notes — posting here so Sara has visibility. 

High-level options to propose to Acme: 
A) H100-only reserved pool 
  - Rationale: best headroom for streaming and large context, lower latency under high concurrency.
  - Rough per-GPU reserved throughput (estimates for a 70B-ish open model, 2048 context, streaming enabled): ~350–450 tokens/sec sustained per H100 (with continuous batching and prefix cache). That maps to ~2k–2.5k concurrent short requests per GPU if average request is small and streaming chunking is efficient.
  - For Acme sustained profile (4200 tokens/min = 70 tokens/sec), you'd need 1–2 H100s reserved to have comfortable headroom for bursts and warm caches; for burst to 120 concurrency we recommend shaping to a 2–3 H100 pool.

B) Mixed pool (H100 primary + A100 fallback)
  - Rationale: cost savings while keeping primary low-latency pool. A100s can act as fallback for lower-priority routes or batch-only workloads.
  - Per-A100 reserved throughput: ~200–300 tokens/sec (depending on kernels/quantization).

Notes / caveats:
- Numbers above are estimates based on our internal perf matrix (see perf_matrix.pdf). Real numbers depend on model family, quantization, output length distribution, and streaming chunk size.
- Warm cache behavior is critical: with prefix/KV caching enabled, p95 streaming latency drops substantially after warm-up; include a 30–60 minute warm-up phase in the validation run.

Proposed validation plan (what we'll run for the July 5 window):
1) Two 12-hour runs (H100-only and A100-only) with the Acme sample workload, with KV cache toggled on/off to measure sensitivity.
2) Collect: per-token latency (p50/p95/p99), time-to-first-token, GPU utilization, token/sec, and tail latencies for streaming chunks.
3) Provide recommended reserved throughput and a production pool sizing with cost estimate and a fallback routing policy.

Action items for us: Dev to draft the validation_run_config.yaml (attached) and propose exact run windows. Marissa to compile cost/options in capacity_plan_v3.xlsx and include mixed-pool scenarios.

Thanks — I’ll be ready for the tech deep-dive as soon as Sara confirms timing.

— Marissa
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Thanks everyone — this looks good and we’re aligned on the approach. A couple of quick asks before we lock in July 5: 

- Confirm you’ll run H100 and A100 sweeps and include per-GPU reserved throughput numbers and cost estimates.
- Please include streaming per-chunk p95 and end-to-end p95. Our UIs care more about token-level TTFB than aggregate completion time. For streaming chunk targets, we want per-chunk p95 <= 80 ms and ideally per-token p95 < 50 ms after cache warm-up.
- We’ll provide the anonymized 24-hour sample workload (attached). We can also provide a small set of golden prompts that must meet deterministic latency targets — I’ll send those tomorrow.

Let’s plan for the July 5 run window. Can you please propose a 2-hour slot on July 5 (your timezone) for a quick kickoff to confirm the harness and metrics? Also please include a HubSpot deal link and a DocuSign preview if there are any PO terms we should expect.

Appreciate it — looking forward to the results.

Best,
